why: This is the best line (p0001) and the most direct route to a high score.
purpose: What single-bump shape maximizes R, and does local search on the height vector from a smooth seed beat 2/3?
plan: Run a general randomized height-improver seeded with a Gaussian; if it gains, keep deepening (larger N, finer search, flat-top seeds); if it stalls, switch to parametric tuning.

why: Cheaply tests whether flat-topped f*f can beat the Gaussian.
purpose: In the exp-power family f=exp(-|2x-1|^p), which p maximizes R — is the Gaussian (p=2) optimal or do flat-top (p>2) profiles help?
plan: Grid p, refine around the best, return the best profile; if p>2 wins open a flat-top thread.

why: Keeps a second, off-best-line source of candidate extremal shapes.
purpose: Do other compact bumps (sin^s, (x(1-x))^α, smoothed box) exceed or match the Gaussian's R?
plan: Score each family across its parameter, report best R and shape; feed the best into future deepens.

why: Core question answered; the open question is now the structural lever (asymmetry/flat top), moved to new threads.
outcome: Yes: general height optimization from a smooth seed beats 2/3 decisively, reaching 0.8034 (p0006).

why: Flat-top beat the Gaussian (0.7437) and may combine with asymmetry.
plan: Develop the flat-top line: take p0005's flat-top profile, upsample, and run direct asymmetric height optimization; if it gains feed back to the best line, if it stalls park the flat-top family.

why: Other parametric bump families (0.7355) are dominated by direct height optimization; lower priority.
Top programs are all asymmetric; this tests the mechanism directly.
purpose: Does deliberately lowering ||f*f||_inf via an asymmetric f (peak suppression) raise R beyond 0.8078?
plan: Apply monotone tilts exp(λ(2x-1)) to the p0004 shape over a λ grid, reoptimize briefly, and plot R vs measured peak; if lower peak correlates with higher R, push asymmetry harder; if not, asymmetry is exhausted.

why: p0004's coordinate ascent is inefficient; a real optimizer may find better optima.
purpose: Does a proper gradient-based optimizer (L-BFGS-B with numerical gradient) beat the crude coordinate/perturbation ascent on the best line?
plan: Run scipy L-BFGS-B on the height vector from multistarts on the p0004 shape; if it beats 0.8078 keep deepening with higher N, else fall back to structural changes.

why: The gain was too small to justify further gradient work.
outcome: L-BFGS-B gave only +0.0008 over the crude ascent (0.808554), so a proper gradient optimizer is not a major lever.

why: p0012's tilt sweep is the best line and has not yet been refined at higher resolution or with targeted peak suppression.
plan: Push p0012 with two distinct mechanisms: mass-preserving multi-resolution refinement at N=1000/2000/4000, and targeted suppression of the f*f peak by local dips; if either gains, continue that mechanism, otherwise shift to the symmetric/multi-scale alternative.

why: p0011's near-symmetric 0.829953 makes this a direct challenge to B2.
purpose: Is asymmetry actually necessary for R above 0.83, or can a symmetrized version of p0012 retain most of its score?
plan: Symmetrize p0012 by averaging with its mirror, optimize under a mirror-symmetry constraint, and compare R and ||f*f||inf; if symmetric R stays near 0.8338, asymmetry is not essential; if it drops, B2 is supported.

why: The flat-top line is far below the best but has not yet been combined with the successful tilt mechanism.
plan: Apply p0012-style monotone tilt and block reoptimization to the p0013 flat-top shape; if it reaches above 0.80, keep the flat-top line alive; if not, park it as noncompetitive.

why: The question is answered and a symmetric line is now worth its own thread.
outcome: Asymmetry is not necessary: symmetrizing p0012 and optimizing under mirror symmetry retained R=0.833835.

why: p0019 shows symmetry is viable and halves the search space.
purpose: Can a symmetric-constrained optimizer push the symmetric shape above the current best 0.837273?
plan: Take p0019/p0018, symmetrize, optimize only half the heights under mirror symmetry at N=1000-2000 with multi-scale block ascent restarts and dip suppression; if it reaches ≥0.837 keep the symmetric line, else park it.

why: Both mechanisms gained independently and should compose.
plan: Combine the two winning mechanisms on p0018: dip suppression at the f*f peak followed by multi-scale block-ascent restarts; in parallel run a random structural-perturbation search (smooth bumps added/subtracted at random locations). If either gains, push that mechanism; else shift to higher resolution.

why: Keep the off-best line alive with the now-proven mechanisms.
plan: Apply p0018-style multi-scale restarts plus dip suppression to the p0013 flat-top shape; if it reaches ≥0.80 keep the flat-top line, else park it.

why: p0025 is the new best 0.838635; continue combined dip suppression + multi-scale restarts on p0025, then add random structural perturbations if it plateaus.
plan: Deepen p0025 with combined peak-dip suppression and multi-scale block-ascent restarts; if a restart fails to gain, run random smooth structural perturbations. Stop after 3 experiments without a real gain.

why: The flat-top exp-power line is still far below the best; give it one final p0018-style multi-scale test before parking.
plan: Apply p0025-style multi-scale restarts and dip suppression to the p0013 flat-top shape; if it does not reach 0.80, park A2.

why: Symmetric search reached 0.833835 but has not yet used the combined winning mechanisms.
plan: Symmetrize p0025/p0018, optimize half-heights at N=1000-2000 with multi-scale block ascent and dip suppression; if it reaches >=0.837 keep the symmetric line, else park.

purpose: Can a compact-support or piecewise-linear nonnegative f with controlled tails exceed 0.838635, testing the tail-limit conjecture?
plan: Construct tent/trapezoid/compact-support profiles with adjustable shoulder and support; optimize heights under fixed support and compare R. If it beats 0.838635, branch from it; otherwise record evidence for the tail limit.

why: p0025, p0022 and p0024 each exploited one of these levers; they have not been combined.
plan: Fuse all winning mechanisms on p0025: strong dip scan (widths 0.02-0.24, amplitudes 0.01-0.12, more refine attempts), then progressive upsampling to N=2000,4000,8000,13000 with block ascent (blocks 8-16) at each level, keeping the global best; if it gains, push N higher and add finer dip widths.

why: p0024's strong dip scan paid; narrow multi-width dips at fine resolution are an untested setting of this mechanism.
purpose: Can fine block sizes (2-6) plus multi-width/narrow dips at high resolution flatten the top of f*f further than coarse dips?
plan: From p0024, resample to N=4000, run block ascent with blocks 2-6 and decaying additive/multiplicative steps, then scan narrow dips (widths 0.01-0.06) at the f*f peak, then resample to N=8000 and polish; if it gains, keep this fine-dip line and push resolution.

why: Symmetric-constrained optimizer (p0020) stayed at 0.833835 with full budget, failing its own >=0.837 keep test; symmetric line is not competitive.
Tests the tail-limit conjecture with a genuinely different construction class.
plan: Explore slot: build compact-support piecewise-linear profiles from scratch (trapezoid with plateau [a,b] and ramp width w, plus optional shoulder), scan parameters, then block-ascent optimize; if any beats 0.838635, branch from it, otherwise record evidence for the tail limit.

why: p0026 and p0029 are complementary strong levers.
plan: Fuse p0029's fine-block (2-6) + narrow-dip (0.01-0.06) stage into p0026's recipe: early polish, tight dip scan, N=4000 fine-block ascent, narrow dip scan, N=8000 polish, growing-N restarts; if it beats 0.839812 keep and push N higher, else fall back to the single strongest stage.

why: p0029 won; test whether the fine-dip line keeps paying at higher N.
plan: From p0029 (N=8000): fine-block ascent (blocks 2-6), narrow dips widths 0.005-0.045, then resample to N=13000 and polish with block ascent + light perturbations; if it gains keep the fine-dip line and push N, else close A9.

why: Compact-support scratch shape only reached 0.801040, far below best; evidence for the tail-limit view.
Flat-top exp-power family stuck near 0.749, far below the best line; not worth further slots.
B8 is untested with the current best recipe; a symmetric line would halve DOF and could be more efficient at high N.
purpose: Can a symmetric-constrained search using the full p0026 recipe match the free asymmetric optimum (testing B8)?
plan: Symmetrize p0026, optimize half-heights with mirror symmetry using polish+dip+block ascent+growing-N restarts; if it reaches within 0.0005 of 0.839812 keep a symmetric line, else record that symmetry restricts.

why: p0037 is the new best and targeted peak suppression has not been tried at N=20000.
plan: From p0037 (N=20000): insert a high-N narrow dip scan (widths 0.002-0.03, amps 0.005-0.04) at N=13000 and N=20000 around the f*f peak, reoptimize top candidates with block ascent, then resample to N=30000-40000 and polish; if it gains keep pushing N and finer dips, else close A4 and fold effort into A9.

why: p0037 used blocks 6-12; very fine blocks at N=20000 are an untested setting of the fine-block mechanism.
plan: From p0037: run very fine block ascent (blocks 2,3,4) at N=20000 with decaying steps and many passes, then resample to N=30000 and polish with blocks 4-6; if it gains keep the fine-block high-N line, else close A9.

why: The thread's keep/park test was met at the tested resolution.
outcome: Symmetric-constrained search with the full p0026 recipe matched the free p0026 optimum exactly (p0035 0.839812), supporting B8; it was not pushed to N=20000.

why: All current lines are local perturbations of similar shapes; a target-driven deconvolution is a genuinely different construction.
purpose: Can direct deconvolution of a flat-top target f*f produce a competitive nonnegative f, opening a construction region different from local height optimization?
plan: Build a flat-top target L (trapezoid/plateau with smooth ramps), initialize h as a box, iterate multiplicative Richardson-Lucy/projected deconvolution for h*h toward L, then run block ascent on R; if it scores above 0.80 keep and develop with dips/upsampling, else record deconvolution as noncompetitive.

why: p0040 showed high-N narrow dips work; now apply them to the new best p0038.
plan: From p0038: insert a high-N narrow dip scan (widths 0.002-0.02, amplitudes 0.005-0.04) at N=20000 and N=30000 around the f*f peak, reoptimize top candidates with fine block ascent; if it gains push finer dips and higher N, else fold effort into A9.

why: p0043 showed fine-block high-N polishing is a distinct lever; p0038 is the stronger base.
plan: From p0038: after its N=20000 multiscale, run fine blocks 2,3,4 with step0 0.05, then resample to N=30000 and N=40000 with blocks 4-6 and polish; if it gains push N=50000, else return to A4 dips.

why: The explore test failed its keep threshold of 0.80.
outcome: Flat-target deconvolution scored 0.791137, well below direct height optimization, so target-driven deconvolution is noncompetitive at this resolution.

why: Branch slot should test a different point on the best line, not another p0038 derivative.
purpose: Can the earlier fork point p0024, reoptimized with the current high-N fine-block/narrow-dip recipe, reach the current best and open an alternative basin?
plan: From p0024, resample progressively to N=2000,4000,8000,13000,20000 with block ascent, then fine blocks 2-4 and narrow dips; if it reaches above 0.8405 keep as an alternate line, else record the fork as noncompetitive.

why: p0045's fine-block stage gained only +8e-5; the fast incremental scorer is the route to finer descent.
plan: From p0045 (N=40000): replace full-convolution scoring with exact incremental delta-convolution score updates (O(N·b) per block move) and run block-1/2/3 coordinate descent for many passes with decaying steps; if it gains ≥0.0001 keep and push to N=60000, else the recipe is saturated at ~0.8410.

why: p0049 shows high-N dips are nearly saturated on p0045; test them in a different basin with the fast optimizer.
plan: From the p0037 fork (peak at 0.573): apply the fast incremental optimizer at N=20000 then resample to N=30000-40000 with narrow dips (widths 0.0005-0.01); if it gains ≥0.0005 keep as an alternate basin, else close A4 as saturated.

why: The branch experiment answered the fork question negatively.
outcome: p0046 reached only 0.838728, far below the 0.8405 threshold, so the p0024 fork is noncompetitive under the modern high-N recipe; rely on the p0038/p0045 line.

why: B9's marginal value of N is falling; this settles where to spend future budget.
purpose: Does pushing N to 60000-100000 with the fast incremental optimizer keep paying, or is high-N saturated?
plan: From p0045: resample to N=60000 and N=80000, polish with fast incremental block descent; if gains ≥0.0001 keep pushing N, else record high-N saturation.

why: The p0037 alternate basin was matured with the modern high-N recipe to 0.840844 (p0055), a gain over its base but still below the main-line best 0.840999. The original peak-suppression question is answered; the alternate basin is noncompetitive.
p0053 at N=60000-80000 gained only +0.000002 and p0054 incremental scoring gained +0.000004: high-N resampling is saturated. Record high-N plateau and stop.

plan: From p0052 (0.840999): run randomized block-order coordinate descent with periodic coarse mass-preserving jumps and keep the best; if it gains ≥0.0001, push to N=60000, else record the plateau as a basin property.
purpose: Can a non-coordinate local search—randomized block reordering with occasional mass-preserving coarse jumps at fixed N=40000—escape the p0052 plateau above 0.8410?

why: B8 is low-confidence and was only tested at low N; a high-N symmetric search is a real off-best-line challenge to whether symmetry restricts the optimum.

purpose: Does a genuinely different multi-lobe/oscillatory nonnegative f, rather than a single-peak height vector, exceed 0.8405 or open a new basin?
plan: From scratch at N=2000-8000, optimize height vectors initialized with two or three separated mass lobes, then refine with multi-scale dips and block ascent; if any candidate beats 0.8405 keep and deepen, else close as noncompetitive.

why: Only non-local moves can leave a coordinate-wise local optimum; this is the cleanest remaining escape mechanism on the best line.
plan: From p0052 (0.840999): fast incremental block-1/2 descent to a local optimum, then repeated non-local mass-preserving jumps (multiply a random 1-5% contiguous region by a random log-factor, renormalize, 2-3 fast sweeps, accept only on improvement) with annealed amplitude; final block-1 polish. If it gains >=0.00005, push hopping to N=60000; else record the plateau as a basin property and close.

why: The C-S argument says mirror symmetry about 0.5 forces a center peak, so the old symmetric thread is reframed around the shifted center the data actually shows.
plan: From p0037: estimate c=argmax(f*f)/(2N), symmetrize h about c, optimize the free half-vector with fast incremental block-1/2 descent at N=20000 for several c in {0.52,...,0.60}, resample the best to N=40000 under the constraint. If it reaches >=0.8405 keep the shifted-symmetry line; if it stays below 0.8395 close A7 as structurally limited.
purpose: Is the optimal f approximately symmetric about a shifted center c!=0.5, and does enforcing shifted symmetry about a free c match or beat the free optimum?

why: Tests whether the single-peak family is the only competitive region before spending more slots on local escape.
plan: From scratch at N=4000: 8-12 random 2-3-lobe initializations, block ascent + narrow dips each, keep the best, upsample to N=12000/20000 with block ascent and dips. If any candidate reaches >=0.8405 keep and deepen; else close A14 as noncompetitive.

why: Two experiments without a real gain and the question is answered.
outcome: Non-local mass-preserving basin hopping at N=40000 gave only +0.000002 (p0060); the high-N local optimum is a genuine basin, but it is now clear the plateau was a recipe artifact, not the problem's ceiling.

why: Plan's keep/park test failed decisively.
outcome: Enforcing shifted symmetry about a free c reached only 0.840232, ~0.001 below the free optimum; f is not well described as shifted-symmetric.

why: Two experiments, both far below threshold.
outcome: Multi-lobe/oscillatory from-scratch constructions reach only 0.800-0.802; the single-peak family is the only competitive region.

why: p0057's entire gain came from this stage; it is the new best line.
purpose: How far does the low-N noisy-restart recipe go — what noise schedule, block sizes and N-growth path maximize it?
plan: From p0057: spend ~80% of budget in a restart loop at N=1250-2500 with annealed noise (0.005-0.06), blocks 8-24, accepting only improvements, periodically resampling the best to N=2000/2500/4000 and continuing restarts. If it gains >=0.0001 keep pushing N growth; else lock the recipe and vary only noise.

why: Branch slot must build off the best line; p0025 is the fork point.
purpose: Is the low-N noisy-restart recipe general (works from other basins) or specific to the p0027/p0057 line?
plan: From p0025 (0.838635, N=1000): resample to 1250, run p0057's dip + grad + long noisy-restart loop with N growth to 2500. If it reaches >=0.8405 the recipe is general and should be applied to every line; if it stays below 0.8395 the recipe is basin-specific.

why: Genuinely different construction: global search in a low-dimensional space rather than local ascent.
purpose: Does a tiny-N (N~200) global random-restart search find a different, better basin than local ascent from a smooth seed?
plan: From scratch at N=200: 100-200 random log-normal/random-piecewise inits, block ascent each, keep top few, upsample 200->500->1250 with block ascent + noisy restarts. If any reaches >=0.8405 deepen it; else record that smooth-seeded local ascent dominates.

why: p0066 is now the best line; the restart recipe should be applied to it, not just p0057.
plan: From p0066 (N=1250): spend ~85% of budget in a noisy-restart + block-ascent loop with N growth 1250->2000->3000->4000, annealed noise 0.005-0.05, block sweep 8-24, narrow dip scan, accept improvements only. If it gains >=0.0002 push N to 6000-8000; else lock N=1250 and vary only noise.

why: p0065 answered the generality question (general, but lower ceiling).
outcome: The low-N restart recipe is general: applied to the p0025 fork it gained +0.001575 to 0.840210, but that fork's ceiling is below 0.8405. The p0027/p0057 line and now the p0066 basin are better; concentrate effort on the best line.

why: p0066 shows the tiny-N global search finds better basins than local ascent; more inits/higher N0 may find an even better one.
plan: Scale up the tiny-N global search that produced p0066: N0=250, ~250 random inits (log-normal, Gaussian bumps, plus downsampled p0066 as one seed), block ascent each, keep top 10, upscale 250->500->1250 with noisy restarts and a longer restart stage. If any candidate reaches >=0.8427 deepen it; else record the tiny-N search saturates at ~0.8426.

why: p0072's own restart stage was only ~10s and ended at 0.852421; a dedicated full polish should extract more from this basin.
plan: From p0072 (N=1250): spend ~92% of budget in a noisy-restart + block-ascent loop (annealed noise 0.008-0.05, block sweep 8-24, occasional N growth 1250->1750->2500), plus narrow Gaussian dips at the f*f peak, accept improvements only. If it gains >=0.0003 push N to 3000-4000; else lock N=1250 and vary only noise/block.

why: p0072 shows the tiny-N global search is the strongest lever and is not saturated; more inits/higher N0 may find yet another basin.
plan: Scale the tiny-N global search further from p0072: N0=320, ~400 inits (log-normal, Gaussian bumps, plus downsampled p0072 and p0069 seeds), block ascent each, keep top 15, upscale 320->600->1250->2000 with noisy restarts, spend last ~40% in restart loop. If any candidate reaches >=0.8535 deepen it; else record the search saturates near 0.8525.

why: A genuinely different construction region: far lower N means far more global coverage per CPU second; may reach basins the N0=250 search cannot.
purpose: Does a very-low-N (N~64) massive global search, where thousands of cheap evaluations are affordable, find better basins than the N0=250 search, then upscale well?
plan: From scratch: N0=64, ~2000 random inits (log-normal, Gaussian bumps, random piecewise blocks), cheap block ascent each, keep top 20, aggressively upscale 64->160->400->1000->2000 with block ascent + noisy restarts. If any candidate reaches >=0.845 deepen it; else record very-low-N saturation.

why: p0079 shows the restart polish of a good basin gains +0.003; p0076 is the best basin and has not had a dedicated long polish.
plan: From p0076 (N=1750): run a cheap single-coordinate polish (~3 s), then a long noisy-restart + block-ascent loop (annealed noise 0.006-0.05, block sweep 8-24, occasional N growth 1750->2500->3000) for ~85% of budget, plus narrow Gaussian dips at the f*f peak. If it gains >=0.0005 push N to 3500-4000; else lock N=1750 and vary only noise/block.

why: Scaling from 250/250 to 320/400 inits gained +0.0038; more coverage may find yet another basin.
plan: From p0076/p0079: scale the seeded tiny-N search further — N0=320, ~600 inits (log-normal, Gaussian bumps, plus downsampled p0076, p0079, p0075), block ascent each, keep top 20, upscale 320->600->1250->2000 with noisy restarts, spend last ~40% in restart loop. If any candidate reaches >=0.8575 deepen it; else record the search saturates near 0.8562.

why: p0075's distinct flat-peak basin (f*f max at 0.398) may hold a different local optimum worth developing.
plan: From p0075 (0.846873): apply the full p0076 recipe — a seeded tiny-N global search (N0=320, inits seeded with p0075) plus upscale 320->600->1250->2000 and a long restart polish. If it reaches >=0.850 deepen further; else record the very-low-N basin tops out below the p0076 line.
